description: Every generated contract file, classified. The contracts are specifications: frozen types and signatures the implementing roles compile against. The only code they carry is the reviewed boundary code listed here, which enforces a requirement at the type boundary (a credential that never prints its token; a confirmation that exists only from a read-back equal to what was written); each producer replaces nothing in it and implements everything else. Generated by requirements-compiler v41 from the contracts it generates and analysis/amendment.json (X17).
typecheck: CI builds contracts/ContractCheck.fsproj; each negative control must fail to compile
stateMachines: X05 proves each machine's states and events are exactly the cases of one interface's unions
materialization: the bootstrap writes each contract into its producer's file, byte for byte, from the same text; two builds are identical (offline suite)

implementation.rationale: The credential type's printed form is fixed to <credential>, so no log, exception or interpolation can show the token. Boundary code: the type is the requirement, not application behavior.
The only constructor of the private credential representation. Boundary code: without it the private type cannot be created at all.

The only way to read the token, as an Authorization header. Boundary code: it is what keeps the token out of every other code path; the negative control ReadCredential.fs proves no other reader compiles.
Read-only accessor of the private confirmation representation. Boundary code: consumers can read a confirmation but never build one.
Read-only accessor of the private confirmation representation (as InvestigationId).
Read-only accessor of the private confirmation representation (as InvestigationId).

The only constructor: a confirmation exists only when the read-back equals what was written (one equality test). Boundary code: it is the type-level form of PERSIST-023; the negative control ForgeConfirmation.fs proves nothing else can create one. The save workflow that calls it is persistence's timed work.
